Scope: phase 1 of the logistics area. Wet networks (sewerage, storm, potable water, fire fighting and TSE, including the force main), dry networks (medium voltage, low voltage, street lighting and telecom), the potable water pump station, the sewage lift station, guard rooms, all road layers up to the asphalt wearing course, and landscape.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 17-Nov-2026 data date the project is 68.4% complete against 86.3% planned, 17.9% behind the plan (SPI 0.79). It gained 3.3% this week against 2.8% planned, so the gap narrowed from 18.3% to 17.9%, the first narrowing in the five weeks shown below.

With 86.7% of the contract time gone, 31.6% of the work remains. Finishing by the contract completion date of 29-Jan-2027 needs about 3.2% a week over the 10 whole weeks left. This week's 3.3% reached that rate for the first time in the five weeks shown, but nearly two-thirds of the man-hours earned this week were testing and commissioning credited to the potable water, fire-fighting and TSE networks (see Data notes). The weekly report's milestone sheet and the P6 update now forecast project handover on 29-Mar-2027, 59 days late, a week later again than last week's forecast. Construction is the weak phase: 57.3% done against 94.2% planned.

Weights are budgeted man-hours. Of the 30,009 man-hours earned this week, about 19,180 (64%) were testing and commissioning on the potable water (+14.0%), fire-fighting (+14.6%) and TSE (+3.9%) networks, which brought potable water and fire fighting close to their plans. Construction gained 2.1%, mostly on the sewerage, storm water and MV networks. Nothing was earned on the sewage lift station or landscape, and the pump station gained less than 0.1%. The P6 update (data date 17-Nov-2026) has 4,851 activities: 2,893 completed, 584 in progress and 1,374 not started. Failed-start activities rose from 1,084 to 1,155.

The P6 update finishes the project on 29-Mar-2027, 59 days after the contract completion date. Most P6 milestones moved another 7 days later with the data date, and construction finish (04-Feb-2027) now falls after the contract completion date. Two networks finish earlier than last week: medium voltage on 27-Dec-2026 (previously 09-Jan-2027) and low voltage on 12-Dec-2026 (previously 14-Dec-2026); the P6 date shown for electrical works is the latest dry-network finish, telecom on 04-Jan-2027. The schedule has no finish constraint at the contract date, so its float is measured against its own late finish. The asphalt wearing course has 5 days of float and construction finish 10 days. Other forecasts in this week's files: 14-Mar-2027 (General Information sheet), 22-Dec-2026 (acceleration plan in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's target date).

Procurement of key materials

Share of each long-lead item delivered to site. Source: weekly procurement update 17-Nov-2026. By discipline (procurement summary in the weekly report), 130 of 160 materials are on site, up from 114 last week: civil and roads 71 of 82, electrical 24 of 30, mechanical 35 of 48.

Street-light cable deliveries resumed5,000 LM of street-light cable arrived (11,054 of 20,000 LM), the only change in the procurement update this week. The weekly report's count of materials on site rose by 16, and 154 of 160 purchase orders are now placed (146 last week).
Pump-station equipment and hydrants still outstandingNothing has arrived of the capacitor banks, MCCs, local control panels, PLC system, level meters or surge tanks, all due 30-Nov-2026, nor of the cranes and fuel pumps due 20-Nov-2026. Only 13 of 82 fire hydrants are delivered against a date of 07-Jul-2026. The delivery finish for street-light poles and cable moved from 15-Nov to 30-Nov-2026. Planned delivery completion: 27-Nov-2026 (electrical), 28-Nov-2026 (mechanical), 09-Dec-2026 (civil and roads). Materials approval: 149 of 160 approved, 2 pending.

Data notes

  • Report week: the weekly report states "Current Contract Weeks: 68 of 78" (Milestones sheet). The report serial number (WPR050) and the consultant's inspection number (50) are not the week number.
  • This-week values compare this report with the 10-Nov-2026 report (previous week folder).
  • Testing and commissioning: about 19,180 of the 30,009 man-hours earned this week are testing and commissioning on the potable water, fire-fighting and TSE networks, and the phase is 40.3% done against 0% planned. The Testing sheet gives these tests "actual" start dates between 11-Jan-2027 and 02-Feb-2027, after the data date, with up to 98% complete; the sheet was also cut from 147 to 51 rows.
  • Four different completion forecasts: 14-Mar-2027 (General Information sheet, −44 days, the same as the Milestones sheet's "ready for initial handover"), 29-Mar-2027 (Milestones sheet and P6 update, −59 days), 22-Dec-2026 (acceleration plan in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's "target" date).
  • The P6 update has no finish constraint, so no activity shows negative float although it finishes after the contract date. 475 in-progress activities have finish dates before the data date (424 last week).
  • Monthly actuals in the Physical-Chart Data sheet were lowered again (May 27.7%, previously 27.9%; July 38.9%, previously 39.1%; September 48.4%, previously 48.7%; October 58.9%, previously 59.1%).
  • Physical progress is 68.40% in the weekly report and 67.80% in the progress presentation.
  • Quantities and man-hours disagree: the potable water network earned 14.0% of its man-hours this week for 142 LM of pipe; Major Quantities shows unit substations and RMUs as fractions (1.33 and 1.34 units installed).
  • The TSE pipe total is 57,419 LM in Major Quantities and 17,678 LM in the Conclusion sheet (88.8% finished there); the presentation's irrigation table gives 26,504 m with the executed length unchanged at 5,053 m.
  • Head count: for November the front page shows 360 planned and 489 actual labour; the Manpower sheet shows 78 and 543, the same 543 as the presentation.
  • Mobilisation: the weekly report gives 30-Aug-2025 as actual, the P6 milestone "Mobilization - Finish" gives 25-Nov-2025.
  • The "Complete earthworks" forecast is 22-Sep-2026, a date that has passed, with earthworks at 96.2%. The "all materials delivered" forecast of 21-Nov-2026 conflicts with 30 of 160 materials not yet on site and delivery completion dates up to 09-Dec-2026.
  • Procurement: the presentation lists 5 RMUs against 3 in Major Quantities, 377 street-light poles delivered against 380 on the lighting slide, 13 fire hydrants against 12, and 330 poles installed against 364 in Major Quantities. The TOTAL row of the weekly report's procurement summary repeats the mechanical row (48 materials, 35 on site). The workbook's procurement log is still unusable.
  • The weekly report's Issues sheet and risk register are empty. The separate risk and issue log is dated 13-Oct-2026, its dashboard shows #REF! throughout, and it uses project ID DAM2-01-029 and names the 3rd and 6th Industrial Cities.
  • NCRs: the front page shows 4 issued and 3 closed; the Quality-Stat sheet and the consultant's submittal log show 57 issued and 55 closed. Shop drawings: 1,774 of 1,774 approved in the weekly report, but 2,126 issued with 13 open in the consultant's log.
  • Sewer pipes are 97.6% finished in Major Quantities, 120.2% in the Conclusion sheet (7,387 of 6,146 LM) and 100% in the presentation (6,257 of 6,257 LM). Potable water pipes are 94.2% in Major Quantities and 83.5% in the presentation; fire-fighting pipes are 101.2% in the Conclusion sheet.
  • Invoicing: the weekly report has 8 invoices (74.7M SAR), invoice 8 not approved by the consultant and none paid; the consultant's log closed invoice 8 on 11-Nov-2026 and the presentation reports 74.7M SAR paid. Contract value is 198,906,162.61 on the front page and 198,906,162.312 "incl. VAT" in the Conclusion sheet. The invoice log has stray values (21,100,000, 20,900,000, 200,000) and EAC shows #REF!.
  • Safety: 13 inductions were given this week but the cumulative count stays at 151 (the bracketed figure rose from 904 to 917).
  • Key submittal dates are in Feb–Mar 2024, before the contract award of 30-Jun-2025. The look-ahead sheet still contains P6 data from the Hail Industrial City Phase II project.
  • The workbook's front page and the presentation also report cost-based progress; this report uses physical progress only.
